summary: Post-market: the risk score closed the day at 45.09, down 1.38 from the previous session, holding at caution with a goldilocks regime. The session's defining feature was severe dispersion across equity groups, with only 9 of 22 sectors/themes closing higher: memory led at 4.5163, semiconductor equipment at 2.6276 and data centers at 1.8803, while quantum computing at -2.2287, AI software at -1.9457 and cybersecurity at -1.8641 lagged. Micron at 1006.97998 (up 3.0159), Broadcom at 355.640015 (up 2.4014) and Nvidia at 219.565002 (up 0.1026) advanced, while Tesla at 362.976013 (-0.8804) fell. Rates still dominated pricing: the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.01 and the 2-year at 4.74, with the real rate at 2.68, both at the 100th historical percentile, and the FedWatch-implied policy rate at 4.165 still points to a hike; this was the first full trading day after the Fed's first rate increase since 2023. Volatility moved the other way, with VIX falling from 17.71 to 15.44, while crypto rose across the board (Bitcoin 81132, up 6.03404; Ethereum 2631.35, up 7.47844; SOL 113.72, up 12.81606), a clear cross-asset divergence. Model confidence 0.9147.

top_risk_drivers.claim: The macro block is the binding constraint at 64.94: the real rate sits at 2.68, the 100th historical percentile, and the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.01 is also in the 100th percentile, making the discount rate itself the main source of risk.

Front-end pricing is still tightening: the 2-year yield at 4.74 widened its premium over the 3.63 effective federal funds rate, the FedWatch-implied policy rate at 4.165 still points to a hike, and the 10-year to 2-year spread is 0.27.
The liquidity plumbing keeps tightening: overnight reverse repo balances are just 0.576 while the secured overnight financing rate rose to 3.85, leaving the money-market buffer very thin.

Internal structure remains weak: semiconductor relative strength at -19.5606 and small-cap relative strength at -5.9568, with just 55.48% of constituents above their 200-day moving average and only 1 new 52-week high among 155 names.

Extreme dispersion inside the AI complex was the session's most striking risk signal: memory led at 4.5163 and semiconductor equipment at 2.6276, while AI software fell to -1.9457 and quantum computing to -2.2287, as capital rotated sharply between hardware cyclicals and software.

supporting_signals.claim: Volatility is the one risk block that clearly improved: VIX fell from 17.71 to 15.44, realized volatility is 9.2068, and the volatility dimension dropped to 18.93.
Crypto shows risk appetite has not retreated: Bitcoin at 81132 (up 6.03404), Ethereum at 2631.35 (up 7.47844) and SOL at 113.72 (up 12.81606).
Memory and semiconductor hardware extended their run: Micron at 1006.97998 (up 3.0159) and Broadcom at 355.640015 (up 2.4014), with the memory theme at 4.5163 and data centers at 1.8803.
Credit markets are not signalling stress: high-yield spreads at 2.7 and investment-grade spreads at 0.78 both remain low.
Trend structure remains constructive: price is 6.2062 percent above the 200-day moving average, only -2.2047 percent below the 52-week high, with 3-month momentum at 1.8735.

contradicting_signals.claim: Cross-asset confirmation is only 0.625, with 6 of 10 signals triggered; equities actually closed slightly lower (SPY proxy -0.2452), which does not square with the collapse in volatility.
Internal model consistency is the weak link: the 0.9147 confidence rests on a consistency factor of just 0.7135 against coverage of 0.93.
The software and consumer-electronics complex weakened across the board, cutting against the goldilocks read: cybersecurity at -1.8641, consumer electronics at -1.8608 and cloud computing at -1.4234.

The A-share memory and semiconductor chain rallied hard the same day, diverging from the weak US AI software complex: 603986.SH up 4.9475, 688825.SH up 3.8713 and 301308.SZ up 3.5423 (these closes come from the 11:30 Dublin A-share close snapshot and are not in this layer's evidence index).

The news layer carries little market signal: the three highest-importance items are Fed enforcement-action notices and reverse repo usage, at importance 59.02, 58.07 and 58.07, offering little macro information to explain the session's sector dispersion.

what_changed_today: The risk score eased to 45.09, a single-day change of -1.38, holding at caution and a goldilocks regime.
Volatility improved materially: VIX fell from 17.71 to 15.44, taking the volatility dimension down to 18.93.
Rates pushed higher: the 10-year yield rose from 5.00 to 5.01 and the 2-year from 4.67 to 4.74.
The real rate rose from 2.62 to 2.68, holding the 100th historical percentile reading.

Leadership rotated to hardware cyclicals: memory at 4.5163 and semiconductor equipment at 2.6276 led, while AI software at -1.9457 and quantum computing at -2.2287 lagged; only 9 of 22 sectors/themes closed higher.
Crypto re-rated: Bitcoin at 81132 (up 6.03404) and SOL at 113.72 (up 12.81606), with risk appetite failing to track the softer equity tape.
watch_next: The FOMC meeting on 2026-09-28: after the first hike, how the committee frames the next step will determine whether front-end pricing extends.
Personal income and outlays (including the PCE price index) and GDP are released on 2026-09-30, the key test of whether disinflation and growth resilience can coexist.
The employment report on 2026-10-02 will decide whether the market must revise hike-path pricing higher once more.
Costco earnings on 2026-09-24: retail demand and cost guidance will test consumer resilience.
Next week's US-China summit is the key hurdle for equities, and the auto industry has written to Trump asking him to bar Chinese automakers from the US market before the summit.

bull_case.title: Bull case: inflation data cooperates and risk appetite keeps repairing
points: If the 2026-09-30 PCE and GDP prints confirm continued disinflation, the real rate could retreat from 2.68 and give valuations room.
Earnings momentum in memory and semiconductor equipment persists; if Micron at 1006.97998 and the memory theme at 4.5163 extend, breadth should repair.
Volatility has already fallen to 15.44, and a low VIX alongside the crypto rally shows risk appetite still has room.

base_case.title: Base case: rates stay elevated and the risk score churns near 45
points: A macro dimension at 64.94 and a real rate of 2.68 at the 100th percentile cap the upside; the risk score is more likely to churn around 45.09.
With the FedWatch-implied policy rate at 4.165 already pricing a hike, marginal moves in front-end pricing rather than overall valuation will drive sector rotation.

bear_case.title: Bear case: the front end pushes higher and breadth deteriorates further
points: If the 2-year yield keeps rising above 4.74 and the real rate breaks past 2.68, valuation pressure would spread from software into hardware cyclicals.

Breadth has not repaired: semiconductor relative strength at -19.5606 and small-cap relative strength at -5.9568, with only 1 new 52-week high among 155 names; if the leading memory and equipment groups give back their 4.5163 and 2.6276 gains, the index has little cushion.
Cross-asset confirmation at only 0.625 shows bonds and equities have not yet priced a common direction.
